# Chronic — Configuration and Passage

## #0 — Two questions about one movement

A synchronic reading holds a configuration together; a diachronic reading follows its formation and transformation. [Symbolon Dynamics](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-symbolon-dynamics/taylor-2026-symbolon-dynamics.md) makes this landscape/trajectory pair operative within objective internality. [C50](../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C50-Dia-Syn.md) distinguishes it from the logical cut/gather pair.

The input is a field with states and possible transitions. A current state is not its entire history, and a succession of states does not by itself state the field's rules.

## #1 — Display the configuration

For an elementary mathematical example, take the map `f(x)=x/2` on the real line. The state-space, update rule and fixed point 0 define one configuration of possibilities. Every real starting value converges to 0 under repeated application. This is a simple attracting fixed point, not a strange attractor.

The synchronic view can state this organisation without choosing one initial value. It holds the possible trajectories together under a specified rule. In the authorial psychic application, a landscape similarly makes active basins, boundaries and available transitions jointly legible, while retaining the distinct warrant required to model an actual psyche.

## #2 — Follow a trajectory

With initial value 8, the successive states are `8,4,2,1,1/2,…`, or `x_n=8/2ⁿ`. With initial value −4, they are `−4,−2,−1,−1/2,…`. The same organisation permits different histories. Neither finite list exhausts the basin, and the basin does not specify which starting point occurred.

If the rule changes during the history, the configuration itself changes. A trajectory can therefore require an account of changing parameters and conditions. The source's objective-internality claim gives memory, tools, affect, institutions and environment constitutive roles: an encounter can alter what becomes available next.

## #3 — Cross temporal and logical readings

| Reading | Retained relation | Severed relation |
|---|---|---|
| Synchronic | Configuration includes its conditions and distinct terms | Opposed terms are displayed with their common condition suppressed |
| Diachronic | Change carries provenance, exclusion and return | Successive determinations conceal the field from which they arose |

This crossing is the page's principal operation. A cut can be productive at either time-scale; a gathering can fail at either. A photograph-like schema is not automatically Syn, and a narrative is not automatically Dia.

## #4 — Distinguish invariance, interpretation and coincidence

An invariant set in dynamics has a technical relation to a specified evolution. An archetypal ordering capacity and its singular manifestations are the source's Argued psychic refraction. The formal example shows how different trajectories can belong to one organisation; it does not establish that every psychological recurrence is governed by a measured dynamical system.

Likewise synchronicity concerns recognised meaning across events with distinct causal histories. Its interpretation requires its own psychic and historical source work. It must not be identified simply with synchrony, a time slice, or a theorem about the fixed point of `x/2`.

## #5→0 — Return the path to the changed field

The result joins two records: what configuration permitted the movement, and what movement actually occurred. A return can then ask whether the field stayed fixed, which conditions changed, and which future transitions the achieved history now enables.

This record returns-to [A13](../../../section-rooms/arguments/A13-Two-Logics-of-Two-Dia-Syn.md), [C50](../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C50-Dia-Syn.md), and [X/x](../ql/x-x.md). [Dia](dia.md) and [Syn](syn.md) operate across both temporalities. The process chain's inverse-phase primes and the quilt's Night-pass primes remain source-local address systems; succession alone gives no licence to collapse them.
